games.name: Rocket League
games.note: Its Easy Anti-Cheat refuses Rosetta's Wine (code 206) and loads its Linux module on the Linux engine. Its publisher executable, Launcher.exe, is a .NET program and the engine's Wine has no Mono: the game starts with the Easy Anti-Cheat bootstrapper Launcher.exe would start, with the same arguments.

games.name: Rocket League
games.note: Its Steam build, which runs as its Epic one. Steam's launch already starts its Easy Anti-Cheat bootstrapper, RocketLeague_EAC.exe. It starts a Steam game server in its own process, which needs Voile v26.3.0-18: in older releases the Linux engine's steamclient.so took that server's threads for dead, and the game closed a second after the anti-cheat's splash.

games.name: ELDEN RING
games.note: Easy Anti-Cheat, as Rocket League's. It only has Direct3D 12, which D3DMetal renders and DXMT does not. Steam's launch already starts its bootstrapper, start_protected_game.exe.

games.name: Fall Guys
games.note: Easy Anti-Cheat, as Rocket League's, with its Linux support turned on. Unity renders it with Direct3D 11, through DXMT as Rocket League. Its publisher executable, RunFallGuys.exe, is a 32-bit .NET program that checks the Visual C++ runtimes and starts FallGuys_client.exe, a 32-bit EOS bootstrapper, and the engine's Wine only runs 64-bit programs: the game starts with the Easy Anti-Cheat bootstrapper those two would start, with the same arguments. Its sockets need Voile v26.3.0-16, whose Linux engine keeps their path MTU options, and its locked mouse the empty clip rectangle that release reads.

games.name: Dead by Daylight
games.note: Easy Anti-Cheat, as Rocket League's: it loads its Linux module on the Linux engine. Unreal renders it with Direct3D 11, through DXMT as Rocket League. Its launch executable, DeadByDaylight.exe, is already the Easy Anti-Cheat bootstrapper. It needs Voile v26.3.0-18: older Linux engines refused its 301st thread and it crashed at start, older Neptune cut its render target calls with a KEEP count short, leaving the screen black, and showed its 10-bit swapchain as 8-bit.

games.name: VRChat
games.note: Easy Anti-Cheat, as Rocket League's, with its Linux support turned on. Unity renders it with Direct3D 11, through DXMT as Rocket League. Its publisher executable, launch.exe, is a .NET program and the engine's Wine has no Mono: the game starts with the Easy Anti-Cheat bootstrapper launch.exe would start, with the same arguments, such as Steam's --no-vr.

games.name: Team Fortress 2
games.note: Picks DirectX level 80 on the GPU Rosetta's Wine reports, where its 64-bit build crashes as each map loads its lightmaps: they overwrite an object of shaderapidx9.dll. Level 95 keeps it on its Direct3D 9 path, which loads maps. Starts through Valve's Windows Steam, whose answer to the game's module signature check lets it join VAC-secured servers.
